key_insight: MedGraph uses graph memory to track changing patient facts across medical conversations while addressing outdated information, person mix-ups, and missing safety facts.
clinical_relevance: More accurate longitudinal memory could help medical dialogue systems preserve patient context across visits, though clinical benefit is not established here.
method: Extract dated facts, identify whom they describe, and link medication, diagnosis, and measurement updates into history-preserving chains.
Retrieve patient-specific chains, interpret them at the requested time, and include original dialogue text.
Include a patient profile containing every recorded safety fact with each question.
evidence_signal: On MedMemoryBench, MedGraph achieved the highest overall accuracy against five baselines with GPT and Qwen backbones, exceeding the strongest baseline by 10.5 and 10.4 points, respectively.
watch_item: Benchmark gains do not establish real-world clinical safety; performance still depends on accurate fact extraction and person attribution.
paper_title: MedGraph: Maintaining Patient State with Graph Memory for Long-Term Medical Dialogue
